newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptians plead not guilty in militants trial.
newsitem.headline: Egyptians plead not guilty in militants trial.

text.p: Ninety-seven Egyptian men and women pleaded not guilty on Wednesday to charges including bombing banks, belonging to illegal organisations and killing the head of the Interior Ministry's anti-militant squad.
It is the largest military trial of Moslem militants in Egypt since the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) took up arms against the government in 1992.

At the Heikstep military base outside Cairo, the military prosecutor read out the charges, which include planting bombs outside nine banks in 1994 and killing police General Raouf Khairat in the same year. Police shot dead two alleged killers.
The trial, which started last Saturday, was adjourned to July 19. It is the first military trial with women defendants.
Several defence lawyers attended the session and some of the defendants asked the court to appoint lawyers for them.
Lawyers say the charges carry sentences from one year in jail for harbouring a fugitive to the death penalty for killing or operating an illegal group.

After heavy security at the opening session, on Wednesday the court allowed the families of the defendants to enter the prosecution cage. Children ran amok in the courtroom while their parents and relatives chatted.
Five of the accused in the trial are being tried in their absence. There were originally 98 in the case but lawyers said one of them died in custody.

Since 1992, the Gama'a and other Moslem militant groups have been fighting to transform Egypt into their version of an Islamic state. Heavy police crackdowns have largely curtailed their activities to sporadic attacks in the country's south.
